commits.author: maobaolong
commits.message:
refactor: rename native_storage_ops to lmcache_native and relocate KV-format/transfer types (#4453)

* refactor: rename native_storage_ops to lmache_native and relocate device-independent KV format/transfer types
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

- Rename the compiled extension native_storage_ops -> lmache_native and
  move EngineKVFormat / GPUKVFormat / TransferDirection and the format
  predicates (is_kv_list, is_layer_list, is_cross_layer, is_mla) into it so
  they are backend-independent single source of truth.
- Add a top-level lmache_native shim and keep a native_storage_ops shim for
  backward compatibility. Forward relocated names from lmcache.c_ops.
- Use absolute include_dirs when building common C++ extensions so the
  engine_kv_format.h include resolves regardless of the build working dir
  (fixes the CPU wheel build under 'python -m build').
- Make the lmache_native top-level shim tolerate a missing native extension
  (CPU-only / test envs) instead of failing the whole import.
- Drop the old native_storage_ops.pyi stub (superseded by the Python shim).

* fix(c_ops): drop lmcache:: prefix for format predicates in storage_manager pybind
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

The format predicates (is_kv_list, is_layer_list, is_cross_layer, is_mla)
live in engine_kv_format.h which has no `lmcache` namespace, so the
`&lmcache::is_kv_list` references failed to compile in the UT build.

* fix(c_ops): drop const on slot_mapping lambdas to match single_layer_kv_transfer signatures
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

The single_layer_kv_transfer / single_layer_kv_transfer_sgl C++ functions
take a non-const torch::Tensor& slot_mapping. The refactor wrapped them in
lambdas that declared slot_mapping as const torch::Tensor&, causing a
'discards qualifiers' compile error. Restore non-const binding.

* fix(c_ops): accept int for lmcache_memcpy_async direction instead of the enum
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

TransferDirection/EngineKVFormat are owned by the lmache_native module only,
so c_ops must not export them. lmcache_memcpy_async was still bound via a raw
function pointer whose 4th param is the C++ TransferDirection type, requiring
a TransferDirection object from the same module. Wrap it in a lambda that takes
an int and casts to TransferDirection, matching the other c_ops bindings and
letting callers pass the enum value (implicitly converted to int).

* refactor: rename storage_manager csrc dir and namespace to lmcache_native
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

Rename csrc/storage_manager to csrc/lmcache_native and the
lmcache::storage_manager C++ namespace to lmcache::lmcache_native
to match the existing pybind module name (lmache_native). Update
build config (setup_extensions/common_cpp.py) and comments.

* fix: avoid duplicate pybind11 enum registration in xpu_ops
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

The SYCL/XPU bindings (csrc/sycl/pybind_sycl.cpp, module lmcache.xpu_ops)
re-registered TransferDirection and EngineKVFormat, which are already
registered by the lmache_native module. pybind11 keeps a global type
registry, so re-registering the same type across modules raises
"type already registered". This surfaced as an XPU CI import error after
the storage_manager -> lmcache_native rename changed import ordering.

Drop the duplicate enum registration and bind the kv-transfer functions
with plain int direction/engine_kv_format args plus static_cast, matching
the c_ops convention. The Python-side GPUKVFormat alias is unaffected.

* Fix typo
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

* Fix typo
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

* refactor: Delete the redundant files.
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

* fix: update origin/dev new test __init__.py files to use lmcache_native
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

origin/dev added three test-level __init__.py files (trace, distributed,
multiprocess) that still referenced the old native_storage_ops module
name. Update them to lmcache_native to match the rename.

commits.author: nayeonikim
commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Bounce unaligned buffers in io_uring uring_cmd read paths (#3891)

Multi-page NVMe passthrough builds a PRP list whose entries must each be
page-aligned. read_uring only enforced this under use_odirect, and
batched_read had no bounce path at all, so unaligned buffers under
use_uring_cmd hit EINVAL on transfers larger than one page.

Extend read_uring's alignment check to use_odirect || use_uring_cmd and
mirror its bounce logic in batched_read. Add 4 env-guarded tests verifying
unaligned read/batched_read, short-buffer bounce, and per-item decisions.
Verified on Samsung PM1753.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

commits.author: 3xdevv
commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Cap uring_cmd auto transfer size by max_segments (#3882)

[Bugfix] raw_block: cap auto max_data_transfer_size by NVMe max_segments

With use_uring_cmd=true, _resolve_max_data_transfer_size auto-detected the I/O split size from max_hw_sectors_kb only, ignoring the device's max_segments scatter-gather limit. The NVMe io_uring_cmd passthrough builds one iovec segment per page, so a transfer larger than max_segments*page_size is rejected by the kernel with EINVAL and every large store/load fails.

Cap the auto-detected size at min(max_hw_sectors_kb*1024, max_segments*page_size), falling back to the max_hw_sectors_kb value when max_segments sysfs is absent.

Signed-off-by: Sangyoon Kwon <syk0905.kwon@samsung.com>
Co-authored-by: Sangyoon Kwon <syk0905.kwon@samsung.com>
Co-authored-by: Zhengfei He <157287166+zhengfeihe@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: 2xdevv
commits.message:
[Fix][NIXL] Report capacity-limited dynamic stores as failed (#4430)

fix(nixl): report capacity-limited dynamic stores as failed

Mark dynamic NIXL store tasks unsuccessful when the capacity check stops a batch. Preserve completed writes and usage accounting while preventing callers from treating skipped keys as persisted.

Signed-off-by: 2xdevv <2xdevv@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: 2xdevv <2xdevv@gmail.com>

With use_uring_cmd=true, _resolve_max_data_transfer_size auto-detected the I/O split size from max_hw_sectors_kb only, ignoring the device's max_segments scatter-gather limit. The NVMe io_uring_cmd passthrough builds one iovec segment per page, so a transfer larger than max_segments*page_size is rejected by the kernel with EINVAL and every large store/load fails.

Cap the auto-detected size at min(max_hw_sectors_kb*1024, max_segments*page_size), falling back to the max_hw_sectors_kb value when max_segments sysfs is absent.

[Fix][NIXL] Report capacity-limited dynamic stores as failed (#4430)

fix(nixl): report capacity-limited dynamic stores as failed

Mark dynamic NIXL store tasks unsuccessful when the capacity check stops a batch. Preserve completed writes and usage accounting while preventing callers from treating skipped keys as persisted.
